page_title: Neural Style Transfer with OpenCV - PyImageSearch

summary.title: Neural Style Transfer with OpenCV
summary.one_liner: You learn how to run pre-trained Johnson et al. neural style transfer models on single images and webcam video using OpenCV's DNN module and Python.
keywords: gatys neural algorithm of artistic style
content loss style loss total variation loss
takeaways: Neural style transfer combines the content of one image with the style of another, using a pre-trained network and a loss function (content, style, total-variation).
Johnson et al. feed-forward models are much faster than the Gatys method but must be trained per style image; the page notes they are up to three orders of magnitude faster.
cv2.dnn.readNetFromTorch loads .t7 models, and blobFromImage with mean subtraction prepares input; output must be reshaped, de-meaned, scaled and transposed for display.
A webcam script cycles through a folder of models with an itertools iterator, switching models on the 'n' key and quitting on 'q'.
summary.summary: The PyImageSearch tutorial explains neural style transfer, contrasting the 2015 Gatys et al. optimization method with the faster 2016 Johnson et al. feed-forward approach and the 2017 Ulyanov et al. instance normalization variant. It then walks through a Python script that loads a Torch .t7 model with OpenCV's DNN module, preprocesses an image blob, runs a forward pass, and post-processes the output for display. A second script applies the same process to webcam frames, cycling through a directory of models with an itertools iterator. The page requires OpenCV 3.4+ and imutils, and includes example timings on a CPU. Much of the closing content is promotional for the author's courses.
